title: Actually: Shakespeare Wasn't Shakespeare?
description: Authorship rumors and stage lore—what’s myth vs. evidence?

questions.question: Myth: Shakespeare dreamed up his love stories. Which of his tragedies retells Arthur Brooke's 1562 poem about two doomed Italian lovers?
questions.explanation: Brooke's poem unfolds over about nine months; Shakespeare crushed it into less than a week. He also made Juliet younger: not yet 14, versus Brooke's 16.

questions.question: Romeo and Juliet wasn't original—roughly how many of Shakespeare's plots were wholly his own invention?
questions.explanation: Scholars usually count just three with no known main source: 'A Midsummer Night's Dream,' 'Love's Labour's Lost,' and 'The Tempest.' The rest borrow from Holinshed, Plutarch, and Italian tales.

questions.question: Almost none of his plots were his own, but his name came in plenty of versions—roughly how many recorded spellings exist?
questions.explanation: Spelling wasn't standardized; records show "Shaxberd" and "Shappere." None of his six surviving signatures spells it "Shakespeare"—doubters love that, but it was normal then.

questions.question: Myth: he always wrote alone. Who co-wrote Henry VIII and The Two Noble Kinsmen with him, then took over as house playwright for his company?
questions.explanation: Together they also wrote 'Cardenio,' a lost play drawn from Don Quixote. Fletcher even wrote a 'Taming of the Shrew' sequel in which Petruchio gets tamed.

questions.question: Doubters say only a university man could have written the plays. What's the highest education Fletcher's famous partner likely received?
questions.explanation: No records survive, but Stratford's school drilled boys in Latin, including Ovid, often called his favorite poet. Ben Jonson still teased that he had "small Latin and less Greek."
